facilityDetails.programFocus: Cedars Textile Arts Collaborative is situated on 22 acres in San Rafael and offers a range of activities and opportunities to earn income through weaving, gardening, cooking, animal husbandry, and art, as well as a senior program. The program aims to foster independence, defend dignity, and realize each person's full potential.

parentReviews: Cedars Textile Arts Collaborative offers vocational training in textile arts, gardening, and animal care for adults with developmental disabilities.
Established in 1982, it provides opportunities for participants to earn income and engage in community art events.
This program is part of Cedars, a nonprofit with over a century of supporting individuals with disabilities.

facilityDetails.programFocus: The CH&S Enterprise Day Program emphasizes a positive behavioral approach to teaching skills and building self-esteem within a structured, engaging, and personalized environment. The curriculum is multi-dimensional, dynamic, versatile, accessible, and ambitious, focusing on vocational, educational, social, and practical skills.

parentReviews: The CH&S Enterprise Day Program supports adults with intellectual/developmental disabilities through a positive behavioral approach.
Established in 1998, it offers structured activities, health monitoring, and therapeutic programming.
As a non-profit, it fosters self-esteem, life skills, and meaningful community participation.

Artists explore fine art, music, and jewelry making, exhibiting and selling their work at the "Artist Within" gallery.

parentReviews: Victory Center (The Cedars of Marin) offers award-winning art programs for adults with developmental disabilities.
Artists create and sell their work at the 'Artist Within' gallery in San Anselmo, fostering community engagement.
The Cedars of Marin has provided services for individuals with developmental disabilities for over 100 years.

parentReviews: Autistry Studios supports autistic/neurodivergent teens and adults in Marin County, focusing on independence through project-based learning.
Founded by parents of an autistic son, it offers therapeutic makerspace workshops and a comprehensive adult program.
As a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, Autistry Studios partners with local businesses like Double Rainbow Cafe for vocational training.
